practitioners.bio: Adrian Voss holds a Master's in Metaphysics and a PhD in Metaphysical Psychology and puts both to work in the most Denver way possible: recurring community sound sessions, including monthly gatherings at Washington Park and First Spiritual Science Church. The practitioner behind Intuitive Sounds (We Are Merkabah LLC) facilitates sound baths with singing bowls, chimes, wave drums, crystal triangles, hand drums, voice, and gong, woven with guided breathwork — "I receive energetic impressions through all the senses," the Intuitive Sounds site explains — alongside intuitive readings and metaphysical coaching.
practitioners.name: Adrian Voss

practitioners.bio: Alana Basamanowicz once described Reiki as "a massage for your aura," which tells you how she talks about this work: plainly, warmly, with a smile in it. Owner of Intuitive Energy Healing in Fort Collins, she is a Reiki Master Teacher, a hypnotherapist trained at the Eastburn Institute of Hypnosis, and a Registered Psychotherapist in Colorado through DORA, and she facilitates sound baths with crystal singing bowls and other instruments — including Sound Bath: A Sacred Start to the School Year at the Timnath Community Room. "Helping you helps me," she told ShoutoutColorado.
practitioners.name: Alana Basamanowicz

practitioners.bio: Amanda Rose keeps Revive Wellness deliberately open-hearted: a Denver sound healing studio at 929 29th Street whose community sound baths are donation-based and timed to the full and new moons, alongside trauma-informed private sessions and corporate events. An intuitive guide facilitating what they call "heart lead healing spaces," they play crystal bowls, Tibetan bowls, drum, and turtle rattle — and Revive's stated mission says it all: inclusive spaces where people can rest, reconnect, and remember their own capacity to heal.
practitioners.name: Amanda Rose

practitioners.bio: Annmarie Fore taught in classrooms for 28 years before sound became her second calling, and she has pursued it the way career teachers pursue everything: thoroughly. Through ResoundingWell in Loveland she offers sound healing sessions, guided meditations, and retreats — playing Himalayan and crystal singing bowls, a planetary gong, monochord, chimes, tuning forks, drums, flute, and her own voice — with diplomas from the Sound Healing Academy and the Medicine of Sound course behind her, and a spiritual director's certification besides. Her sign-off says the rest better than we can: "Only love, friends, so all may live resounding well."
practitioners.name: Annmarie Fore

practitioners.bio: "I don't simply play these instruments," Ann Martin says. "I compose with them." A Centennial musician, composer, and self-described Acoustic Harmony Specialist performing as Mile High Healing Vibe, she layers quartz crystal and metal singing bowls, gongs, and flute into composed harmonic soundscapes shaped by the room, the moment, and the people gathered. She created the BLISSbowls singing bowl training series and teaches it internationally — and you can catch her regularly at 5 Star Salt Caves' Sound Concerts and at Denver Botanic Gardens.
practitioners.name: Ann Martin

practitioners.bio: Beth Naumann is an artist in the fullest sense — her practice spans sculpture, end-of-life care and exploration, and sound-based wellness with the gong. At Una Vida Meditation & Movement in Niwot she leads Deep-relaxation Gong Sessions where participants lie down or sit and simply receive, played on a Paiste Synodic Moon Gong — an instrument tuned, as the studio tells it, to the frequency of the moon's travel around Earth.
practitioners.name: Beth Naumann

practitioners.bio: Thirty years of teaching movement — ballet, barre, a Master Trainer post at Pure Barre — gave Brookelin Barnhill her foundation; certifications in breathwork, sound healing, Reiki, EFT tapping, and meditation built the rest. "Our breath is one of the most powerful medicines we possess," she writes, and her Breath & Sound: Monthly Journey at Sacred Society puts that belief to work: seventy-five minutes of breathwork and sound bath on the first Sunday of each month, practicing as Breathe with Brookelin.
practitioners.name: Brookelin Barnhill

practitioners.bio: Chavon co-hosts community sound baths in downtown Colorado Springs at The Next Us, alongside co-facilitator Diane of Soothing Frequencies LLC — and the instrument list alone is worth the trip: crystal singing bowls, bronze singing bowls, gongs, chimes, harp, flutes, and hand pan. Zero-gravity chairs await early registrants, and the gatherings are community-first: easy to join, often free or by donation.
practitioners.name: Chavon

practitioners.bio: Christina Epps moves between two worlds most people keep separate: she founded Craft Fitness Denver as a NASM-certified personal trainer and Women's Fitness Specialist, then went just as deep the other direction — a 1000-hour holistic health practitioner certification in San Diego and certification as a Sound Healing Alchemist. Her stated focus is "low impact, high intensity fitness as well as ancient relaxation practices" — strength and stillness from the same hands. At Sacred Society she leads Stretch & Sound and the Sound Bath: Restorative Experience, and she hosts sound baths around Denver.
practitioners.name: Christina Epps

practitioners.bio: Courtnee Ghosh teaches Feng Shui the practical way — organized around the areas of the Bagua Map, with take-home rituals — and then lets a sound bath do the settling. Her Feng Shui Sound Bath events with The Oracle Collective at Firiel Skin Care in Lafayette pair the teaching with a restorative sound bath of crystal singing bowls, chimes, and other instruments: a House Therapist with a session built for both your home and your nervous system.
practitioners.name: Courtnee Ghosh

practitioners.bio: Cyndi Ortiz spent 20 years as a senior producer in TV and film before burnout — and her recovery from it — turned her toward this work, and Liminal Lemonade is what she built on the other side: an Earth Medicine practice drawing on her Puerto Rican and Taino ancestry and the intuitive gifts of both her grandmothers. Her trainings include Usui Reiki Level 2, sound healing certification, The Embody Lab's Integrative Somatic Trauma Therapy program, and life coaching. "Liminal space is not something to rush through," she writes — "it is a time to be honored."
practitioners.name: Cyndi Ortiz

practitioners.bio: Danielle Grace built My Strength Tank around a disarmingly simple inventory — five "Life Tanks": finances, fun, mind, health, and relationships — and she has worked in health and wellness entrepreneurship since 2007. A somatic breathwork facilitator in Colorado Springs, she guides rounds of circulatory breathing designed to release stored stress and emotion, and her invitation is direct: "your breath is powerful." At Singing Bowls of the Rockies she co-facilitates Somatic BreathWork & Sound Bath sessions, her breathwork carried on the studio's live sound.
practitioners.name: Danielle Grace

practitioners.bio: Dawn Stratton plays in the Harmonic Quintessence — Discover Your Spiritual Gifts' five-practitioner sound immersion group — and co-facilitates the center's Sacred Sound Baths with Vialet Rayne in Centennial. Her page here grows as we learn more; her sound is already on the calendar.
practitioners.name: Dawn Stratton

practitioners.bio: Deborah Green's path has the shape of a life honestly lived: a BSc in Psychology, yoga teacher trainings in 2003 and again in 2018, a breathwork master certification, meditation teaching, ICF wellbeing coaching, and sound bath facilitation. She writes that what carried her through her 20s and 30s "is not what has got me through my 40's onwards." Practicing as Deborah Green Wellbeing in Denver, she centers her sound baths on crystal singing bowls, Koshi wind chimes, and tuned chimes, offered to groups and in private 1-to-1 sessions — and at Sacred Society she leads the Sound Bath: Sacred Rest Ritual.
practitioners.name: Deborah Green

practitioners.bio: Elise Nicole Kirkpatrick runs the rare sound bath you attend from a hammock: her Floating Sound Bath at Camino Wellness Sanctuary in Colorado Springs cocoons participants in silk aerial hammocks — cushioned mat spots wait for anyone who prefers the floor — while she guides a meditative sound bath framed as a grounding reset and a chance to set a path and intention for healing. She also works as a mentor in authenticity and embodiment practices.
practitioners.name: Elise Nicole Kirkpatrick

practitioners.bio: Gigi Martins, PsyD, spent a career as a psychology professor and psychotherapist before founding Singing Bowls of the Rockies in Colorado Springs — which may explain why her studio's sessions are designed, in its words, around "the interplay of frequencies, vibrations, and positive energy within a safe and nurturing space." A certified sound bath practitioner since 2015, she plays from a collection of more than 100 crystal and Tibetan singing bowls, plus chimes, tingshas, flutes, drums, hand pans, and tuning forks. No venue puts more sessions on this calendar than hers.
practitioners.name: Gigi Martins

practitioners.bio: Jessica Stokes practices in many keys at once — author, teacher, energy healer, intuitive belly dance instructor, women's retreat facilitator. Her sound baths bring crystal singing bowls, chimes, drums, and traditional flute; her healing practice blends Reiki, Therapeutic Touch, sound healing, and Daoist Stone Medicine; and she plays in the Harmonic Quintessence sound immersion group. Find her at Discover Your Spiritual Gifts in Centennial, where she sees clients on Thursdays.
practitioners.name: Jessica Stokes

practitioners.bio: John "ThunderHeart" Robinson has spent decades in this work — over 30 years in martial arts, 15 years of sacred sound, and a long practice of guiding meditation, energy healing, drumming ceremonies, Reiki, and shamanic practices across Colorado. His sound journeys weave Native American flute, buffalo drum, djembe, didgeridoo, and rattles into what his listings call an earthy, deeply meditative atmosphere, and he leads Shamanic Sound Journey meditations with The Inner Light Center of Colorado Springs.
practitioners.name: John ThunderHeart Robinson

practitioners.bio: "My name is Joy, a name I strive to live up to!" — that is Joy Childress introducing herself, and the rest follows suit. A Fort Collins yoga teacher (200-hour, 2015), Usui Reiki Level 3 practitioner, astrologer, and artist with a BFA from Colorado State, she calls herself an Energy Alchemist and leads heart-opening yoga paired with sound bowl healing on her set of seven bowls — including nature-based sessions like the yoga and sound bath gatherings at Camdazco Farm near Boulder.
practitioners.name: Joy Childress

practitioners.bio: Kathy Sietos grew up with the mystical traditions and herbal medicines her Greek immigrant parents carried to the United States, and more than twelve years ago she planted her own tradition on South Pearl Street: Green Light Reiki. A Reiki Master Teacher, Certified Sound Therapist, Yoga Instructor, Meditation Facilitator, and Licensed Massage Therapist, she leads sound immersions that draw on gongs, bowls, drums, and other instruments — a dozen years of Denver healing practice in every session.
practitioners.name: Kathy Sietos

practitioners.bio: Kochun-Ra came through strong fear and depression and now, in their own words, sees the wonder in life — and wants to share the happiness they found. Their 45-Minute Reset at Inca Street Collective in Denver's Santa Fe Arts District stacks sound, movement, breath, and laughter into three-quarters of an hour, built on what their profile describes as learning "every day how to listen, laugh, love and be with everything in life."
practitioners.name: Kochun-Ra

practitioners.bio: Laura Riehman brings a whole orchestra to Niwot — gong, alchemy and quartz crystal bowls, Tibetan bowls, Native American flute, and more — as a shamanic practitioner, sound healer, and reiki master at Una Vida Meditation & Movement. Her Sound Bath Ceremonies are offered, in the studio's own words, as a peaceful space for stillness, clarity, rejuvenation, and connection, and she also co-leads combined breathwork and sound bath ceremonies there.
practitioners.name: Laura Riehman

practitioners.bio: Megan Odom is a Reiki practitioner in the Colorado Springs area and a lovely presence at Singing Bowls of the Rockies: while the studio's crystal bowls and chimes fill the room, she moves quietly from person to person offering individual Reiki energy work — a session inside the session. Her page here grows as her calendar does.
practitioners.name: Megan Odom

practitioners.bio: Meg Munster's day job is precision — a licensed massage therapist, educator, and movement professional with nearly a decade of anatomy-grounded bodywork: structural integration, craniosacral therapy, lymphatic support. Once a month the studio becomes something else: Vibrations of Peace, a gong bath and sound immersion at Mile High Mindfulness and Massage in Greenwood Village, layering crystal and brass singing bowls with a 26-inch gong, breathwork, meditation, and essential oils — and it ends, wonderfully, with a community tea social so the experience can settle. The studio describes itself as a safe, inclusive, affirming space for all bodies and identities.
practitioners.name: Meg Munster

practitioners.bio: Norabell Dechant founded Pursuit of Vitality in Loveland and says it plainly: it "was never just a business venture — it was a calling." An energy and integrative health practitioner, they offer sacred sound healing ceremonies alongside craniosacral therapy (newborn work included), reflexology, Jin Shin, and somatic emotional energy release — and they keep community sound gatherings going month after month, including a monthly sound bath at Verdant Nature Creations in Loveland.
practitioners.name: Norabell Dechant

practitioners.bio: Norma Groverland opens Unity of Boulder's Wednesday evening meditation and prayer gathering with her own chanting and leads its healing-prayer portion, co-holding the evening with Jack Groverland; on Sunday mornings she performs live Tibetan singing bowls for the center's meditation and satsang. The gatherings rotate through crystal and Tibetan bowls, native flute, and meditative chanting — and they are free, with donations accepted, week after week.
practitioners.name: Norma Groverland

practitioners.bio: The Colorado Psychedelic Church's clergy page calls Oracle Richard "a bridge between the seen and unseen," and notes something rarer: he does not offer answers — he helps people ask the right questions. A clergy member working with natural medicines and metaphysical insight, with a stated commitment to accessibility "especially for those harmed by traditional systems," he leads the church's Communal Quartz Sound Bath in Colorado Springs on first Mondays: an hour of being carried by the hum of quartz, then a quiet reintegration with optional sharing.
practitioners.name: Oracle Richard

practitioners.bio: Pavanjeet's biography says their teaching "balances the profound with light-hearted play," and the résumé backs both halves: Kundalini Research Institute certification (Levels I and II), Master Gong Practitioner Training with additional Gong Therapy certification, teenage years already deep in yoga and astrology, and seasons lived in Indian ashrams. Their six-gong sound baths land at The StarHouse and North Boulder Park — and online — carried by a practice that also holds Kundalini Bodywork and Core Synchronism certifications. Boulder suits them.
practitioners.name: Pavanjeet

practitioners.bio: Ray Ringsel works under a name that tells you what she believes — Wise Innocence — and she told VoyageDenver the heart of it: healing "is about remembering who you've always been beneath the conditioning." A Denver trauma-informed coach and licensed NLP practitioner, she blends NLP, somatic coaching, breathwork, and sound healing with a focus on nervous system regulation. At Sacred Society in the Highlands she leads the NLP Soundbath Experience, pairing guided NLP work with live sound — talk-work and sound-work in one evening.
practitioners.name: Ray Ringsel

practitioners.bio: Sage Love holds a Master of Theological Studies from the Iliff School of Theology and a healing practice called PrayerCraft — the name is the philosophy. On second Saturdays she leads the Sound Bath, Meditation & Community Circle at Brookstone Recreation Center in Loveland, organized with Citrine Unlimited, blending sound healing, guided meditation, ritual, and trauma-informed practices — crystal singing bowls, a tongue drum, and a rain stick may all make an appearance. She is also a published author.
practitioners.name: Sage Love

practitioners.bio: Sharay built Soul Light, LLC around a simple aim: "connecting people to themselves, each other, and the natural world" across the Pikes Peak Region. Offering Reiki, sound relaxation, guided meditations, and energy-healing education from Colorado Springs, Sharay also hosts the Circles of Connection series at La Foret in Black Forest through the Soul Light Community Wellness Foundation — gatherings that braid a relaxing sound bath with Medicine Wheel teachings, nature walks, and guided reflection.
practitioners.name: Sharay Fay

practitioners.bio: Shelby Moor keeps The Denver Village in Aurora on a lunar schedule — a recurring series of moon-cycle sound baths spanning Buck Moon, Harvest Moon, Pink Moon, and Snow Moon editions. The hour-long gatherings are described as "a gentle, immersive journey of healing tones and soothing vibrations," and Moor is the organizer who keeps them coming, moon after moon.
practitioners.name: Shelby Moor

practitioners.bio: Tammy Hopkins carries one of the widest toolkits at Discover Your Spiritual Gifts in Centennial — massage therapy, psychic mediumship, hypnotherapy, Reiki, tarot, spiritual coaching, and Ancestral Regression Therapy (ART), a practice she founded herself. She plays in the Harmonic Quintessence, the center's five-practitioner sound immersion group, and sessions with her are by appointment.
practitioners.name: Tammy Hopkins

practitioners.bio: Terri Slezak's self-description — "Trauma-Informed NLP Life Coach & Intuitive Healer" — only covers half of what they give Boulder County: they also organize free community AcuDetox clinics (a gentle ear-acupuncture protocol for stress release) and sound bath experiences open to all. The through-line is access: wellness events built so that anyone can walk in.
practitioners.name: Terri Slezak

practitioners.bio: Tom Janecek received his Reiki 1 attunement in 1988 — he has been at this longer than some practitioners have been alive — and the decades since have added Usui Reiki Master training, Angelic Reiki certification, Shamanic Practitioner training at Sacred Hoop Ministries, and affiliate membership in the International Center for Reiki Training. Founder of Open Wings Reiki on Manitou Avenue in Manitou Springs, he leads shamanic drumming journeys and co-facilitates Shamanic Sound Journey events with John ThunderHeart Robinson.
practitioners.name: Tom Janecek

practitioners.bio: Vialet B Rayne founded Discover Your Spiritual Gifts in Centennial and filled it with sound: she organizes and plays in the center's Sacred Sound Baths and the five-practitioner Sound Immersion with the Harmonic Quintessence, practicing Divine Sound Healing alongside Angelic Reiki (Master Teacher), Akashic Records reading, and spiritual mentorship. The road there ran through a Master's in Human Resource Development, a decade-plus as a college professor, more than 60 self-published books, and founding the Sacred Temple Mystery School in 2017. "Sacredness is the dedication and devotion of holding divine space," she writes — and she built a whole center for it.
practitioners.name: Vialet B Rayne

practitioners.bio: Zach Miller's site puts it simply: sound has "been my way of connecting with the Divine for as long as I can remember." Through Sound Wave Sacrament, Miller serves Fort Collins and Northern Colorado as a certified sound healing practitioner — crystal singing bowls, Tibetan metal bowls, gongs, chimes, and percussion — describing the work as holding space for people who want to bring healing, growth, and spiritual transcendence into their lives, and the practitioner as "a student constantly in a state of learning."
practitioners.name: Zach Miller
